title: Price Accordion: HC Gamma Probe (Sept 2025)
summary: Experiment document for a staggered pricing-and-capacity playbook ("price accordion") that ties incremental price bands to headcount provisioning rules. Goal: find minimal HC delta that preserves margin under downward price drift while enabling controlled demand capture on upward price moves. This is not the final pricing policy — it is a probe to collect data and a runbook for Q4 price sensitivity experiments.
assumptions:
1) Baseline token mix and cost: hosted API avg token cost = $0.00045/token (current mix), median seq len 350 tokens per request.
2) Elasticity buckets: low-sensitivity enterprise (-5% demand per -10% price), mid-sensitivity SMB (-20% demand per -10% price), high-sensitivity dev/experimental (-40% demand per -10% price).
3) HC ramp lead times: Eng/SRE hiring 10 weeks; CS/AM hiring 6 weeks; Support hiring 4 weeks.
4) Productivity offsets: batching/quantization improvements estimated to deliver 8–12% unit cost reduction if implemented across serving runtime (assume realized over 6 weeks).
5) Reserve pool: 10% of GPU capacity held as burst; cost of burst billed at weighted spot premium of 1.4x normal unit cost.

headcount_notes:
- Baseline FTE includes 1.5 months of hiring buffer to hit Q4 projected usage.
- Upside scenario assumes +35% sustained volume growth and push for Dedicated capacity onboarding requiring 1.2x more SRE/eng to maintain latency SLO.
- Downside scenario is price-compression (20% realized price drop) where we delay non-critical hires and freeze contractors first.
- Cost per FTE uses region-weighted averages and employer burden (benefits + payroll tax).

Price band | Relative price vs baseline | Expected demand delta (weighted) | Unit margin change | Net revenue delta | HC delta to stabilize margin
Band A (protect) | -20% | -10% | -18% margin | -15% rev | -12 FTE (defer hires + contractors)
Band B (defensive) | -10% | -6% | -9% margin | -7% rev | -6 FTE
Band C (base) | 0% | 0% | 0% margin | 0% rev | 0 FTE
Band D (capture) | +10% | +8% | +12% margin | +9% rev | +8 FTE
Band E (aggressive) | +25% | +20% | +30% margin | +23% rev | +20 FTE
sensitivity_methodology:
- Demand sensitivity modeled with segmented elasticity per customer tier (enterprise, mid-market, developer).
- Unit cost model includes GPU amortization, electricity, networking, and SRE ops overhead.
- Margin delta computed after reclaiming 20% of API latency-related refunds and accounting for reserved vs burst GPU mix.
- HC delta is the staffing change required to keep gross margin within +/-3 percentage points vs baseline given revenue change, factoring in partial contractor swaps and 60-day hiring lag for engineers.
conclusions:
1) Small downward price moves (-10%) can be absorbed by operational levers (quantization, batching) and delaying non-critical hires; still recommend a 6 FTE hiring pause as first line of defense.
2) Upward price moves (+10% to +25%) justify front-loading SRE/eng hiring to keep latency SLOs; marginal ROI is highest for SRE hires in Dedicated onboarding windows.
3) The "accordion" approach (pre-defined price bands with explicit HC actions) reduces decision latency and gives sales/AMs clear guidance on discounts/commitment swaps.
4) Recommend a 6-week probe (A/B pricing routes) instrumented with token-level margin telemetry and a hiring gating workflow in Lever/Jira so we can observe real elasticity and update the HC deltas.
open_questions:
- How correlated is short-term spike demand with enterprise committed churn risk? Need cohort analysis for customers with support-intensive integrations.
- Can we accelerate quantization rollouts into Production to recover 8–12% unit cost inside a 4-week window? Engineering ETA variance is high.
- What contractor vs FTE mix yields better elasticity coverage for Q4? Cost-per-hour vs ramp time trade-offs need a table from People Ops.
- Legal/pricing compliance: do banded discounts require updated T&C or a single signed addendum for certain regions?

notes:
Notes to self: capture granular telemetry for at least 3 weeks before making any hiring offers tied to Band D. This doc is intentionally prescriptive so sales and ops don't stall in the face of rapid price movements. Keep experiment windows short and instrumented. Use the 'reserve pool' only after HC gating thresholds are hit.

Rough micro-calcs (back-of-envelope): a sustained +10% price across current mix yields ~+$1.2M ARR lift (net of marginal compute) which funds ~5 additional engs (12mo) or 22 support hires (12mo) depending on mix. Validate with full model export (sheet) before committing hires.
